cues.text: Before the titles, there was a boy and a courtyard. He knew its horses better than its promises.
He came home alive. The names behind the attack did not come home with him.
The coins in his purse were not the wealth of the household. Behind its walls were mouths that would need feeding again.
A load had a price. The road, he would discover, had terms of its own.
He gained passage by acknowledging another household's claim. The road was open; the claim was not forgotten.
The answer came through another man's voice. It offered passage today, not certainty about tomorrow.
He left the claim unsettled and chose the longer ground. Distance, too, had its cost.
The load was home. Only now could a promised supply become food in the store.
